newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends flat vs dlr, forward premia fall.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends flat vs dlr, forward premia fall.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Wednesday at 35.83/835 per dollar, little changed from the day's opening quotes of 35.83/84, dealers said.
They said dollar buying by a large state-run bank and some Bombay-based companies pushed the rupee down to 35.86 briefly before it staged a rally on improved supplies of the US currency.
"Some banks unwound long positions as the rupee slipped and this improved dollar supply," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
The rupee traded at a high of 35.825 per dollar and a low of 35.86 on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) bought dollars at 35.835 rupees, up from Tuesday's 35.82.
"But it (RBI) was not really hitting the market," said a dealer. "It was basically mopping up excess dollar supplies."
Dealers said forward premia fell on receiving pressure from the RBI. They said the RBI rolled over December-maturity swaps receiving premia on December over June dollars.
The annualised premia on six-month dollars ended Wednesday at 7.37 percent against Tuesday's close of 7.71 percent.
